title: Allowlisted precompiled worker module loader
objective: Load the explicitly precompiled maximal-order worker module graph in lightweight multiprocessing evaluators without a parser, compiler, or arbitrary filesystem lookup, and reject unknown or uncompiled modules with Windows/SEA-safe fallback semantics

handoff.summary: Added a fail-closed resource manifest and lazy loader for build-precompiled multiprocessing modules, an exact read-only capability query, portable virtual filenames, and focused synthetic loader/rejection coverage. Ordinary builds without the optional graph retain self-contained Pool behavior and report the module capability as false.
risks: The declared nf-maxorder-public-worker dependency is not yet committed on this base, so the real local_parallel_worker graph and x^2-8 Pool integration require validation after integration.
The full multiprocessing test passed 9 of 10 cases here; its advanced elliptic case requires the optional FLINT addon, which this isolated worktree does not have installed.
next_steps: After integrating nf-maxorder-public-worker, run pnpm python:precompile:run and the focused public Round2 worker test.
Run the full multiprocessing suite in a prepared native worktree and exercise the emitted graph in a SEA/Windows build.
